criteria.rationale: Almost everything is checked against the digest or gated. iOS floor 18 means promptsForUserConfiguration, Controls and ControlCenter need no gates. The watchOS 10 floor gates the newer APIs correctly: AccessoryWidgetGroup and handGestureShortcut sit behind `if #available(watchOS 11.0, *)`; recommendations() returning [] is behind watchOS 26; watch Controls use `#if compiler(>=6.2)` + `@available(iOS 18.0, watchOS 26.0, *)` + `if #available` in the bundle. It spots a subtle trap: on iOS, `#available(watchOS 26, *)` is true through `*`, so that check lives only in the watch folder. Per-platform same-named types (PlatformWidgetConfig, QuickLogView, platformPrompt()) keep .systemSmall off watchOS and .accessoryCorner off iOS. recommendations() is always implemented. The control closure uses only `let` plus one ControlWidgetButton. openAppWhenRun, supportedModes, iOS 27 APIs, HKCorrelation, HealthKitUI and AppIntentsPackage are banned, and a path-scoped lint enforces it. requestAuthorization compiles only under SAYONE_APP, so no extension can compile it. Capabilities are only HealthKit and App Groups, with no Siri, iCloud or Push, so a free team can sign. XcodeGen 2.46.0 is pinned, the generated project is committed, Linux runs a preflight grep on the pbxproj phases and schemes, SWIFT_VERSION is 5.0 and strict concurrency is minimal. The CI matrix builds all 4 schemes with fail-fast false. I compiled `#if compiler(>=6.2) && !FLAG` inside a result builder and `#if os(iOS) && FLAG` with Swift 6.4; both parse. Two gaps. (1) WatchConnectivity (sendMessage/transferUserInfo/updateApplicationContext, iOS-only delegate methods) is used but is not in the digest; §19 says so itself. It is on a non-critical path and can be compiled out with SAYONE_NO_WC, which is ON by default and is a custom flag, not #available or #if compiler. From my own experience the calls exist and the iOS-only delegate methods are correctly put under `#if os(iOS)`. Still, this matches the partial anchor word for word: 'one unverified API on a non-critical path'. (2) A target-membership compile error that the anchors do not cover: `primaryHandGesture()` is defined only in watchOS/App/HandGesture.swift, but §10 uses it in the watch widget's rectangular view. The SayoneHealthWatchWidgets sources (watchOS/Widgets, WidgetShared, Shared/*) do not include watchOS/App, so that target will not compile until the helper moves. I list it as must_fix, not as an anchor downgrade. Score: partial.

criteria.rationale: Every C5 element is present and concrete. (a) App Shortcuts with Russian and English phrases: §12.2 lists 6 AppShortcuts with en and ru phrase lists, generated into AppShortcuts.xcstrings stringSets from shortcuts.tsv. Each phrase has ${applicationName} exactly once and at most one parameter, including gendered forms for the watch's exact matching. (b) Parameterised by preset and drink: LogPresetIntent takes a DrinkPresetEntity and LogBeverageIntent a BeverageEntity, both AppEntity. suggestedEntities() is implemented. updateAppShortcutParameters() is called in App.init and after every catalog change. (c) Runs without opening the app: no intent declares openAppWhenRun or supportedModes, and authenticationPolicy stays at the default .alwaysAllowed. (d) On the watch: SayoneShortcuts, the Siri intents and AppShortcuts.xcstrings are compiled into the watch app, which carries HealthKit, and check_appintents.py asserts autoShortcuts in the watch app's extract.actionsdata. (f) No SiriKit: it says explicitly no com.apple.developer.siri, no NSSiriUsageDescription and no Intents extension, and the lint forbids the entitlement. There is a minor usability risk: runtime preset titles like «Вода 500 мл» are in the nominative, so «Запиши ${preset}» reads awkwardly. customTitle mitigates this, and it does not break any anchor. criteria.rationale:
I checked all five properties against the text.

(1) Idempotent HealthKit writes. Every sample carries HKMetadataKeySyncIdentifier "<entryUUID>.<kind>" plus SyncVersion NSNumber(1). The flush does not rely on the undocumented result of an equal-version re-save: it first runs hasSamples(entryID:) (HKSampleQueryDescriptor with a SayoneEntryID metadata predicate, limit 1) and saves only if nothing is found. Concrete mechanism.

(2) No watch/phone double counting. The single-writer rule says only entry.origin == DeviceOrigin.current writes or deletes samples, and peer entries are stored as .remote and never written. The WatchConnectivity and HealthKit-import paths both merge by UUID. Totals come only from the local store, never from a HealthKit sum. A 2 s dedupe runs inside the flock-locked mutate, so two processes cannot both append. Concrete.

(3) Undo/delete removes Health samples. There is a pendingDelete state and deleteObjects(of:predicate: SayoneEntryID == id) per writable kind. Remote entries are tombstoned and routed over WC to the origin device, which deletes when it merges. The flush retries pendingDelete. Concrete.

(4) Locked-device and extension writes are not lost. The tap is journaled first (append .pending under lock) and HealthKit is tried afterwards. The file uses the default protection class, not .complete. Controls and Siri keep authenticationPolicy .alwaysAllowed. errorDatabaseInaccessible stops the flush and it retries on the next activation. The apps flush on launch, on every .active and after authorization. Concrete.

(5) Totals converge. Each device keeps its own store. WC sendMessage/transferUserInfo carries deltas and tombstones, updateApplicationContext carries a snapshot, and HealthImporter backfills own samples from the last 2 days by metadata. SyncMerge merges by UUID with LWW by modifiedAt, and every change triggers widget reloads. Concrete. Convergence is only eventual and is gated on an app running: entries logged in a widget extension reach the peer only when an app opens. The proposal states this limitation openly.

Weaknesses found. None removes a property, but several are real bugs:
- Race between undo and an in-flight save in another process. The undo deletes 0 samples and marks the entry .deleted. The save then completes, and markHealth(.saved) lands on a tombstoned entry, so the sample survives. The proposal claims 'pending as pendingDelete covers a save racing', but its delete-then-mark-deleted sequence does not.
- applyImported does not say what modifiedAt imported entries get. If an import timestamp is used, a later-arriving WC tombstone could lose the LWW comparison.
- prune (run on every mutate, 7-day tombstone and 60-day retention) is not stated to keep pending/pendingDelete entries. It could drop a Health delete that never ran.
- The 2 s dedupe keyed on (beverage, volume, source) also applies to source .app. A deliberate double tap on the same tile in the app would silently lose the second drink.

All five properties have concrete mechanisms, so the pass anchor is met. I mark it ambiguous because convergence depends on an app being opened.

criteria.rationale:
Module boundaries are explicit and diagrammed in §3.
- SayoneCore is a Foundation-only package that tests on Linux.
- Shared/Platform, Shared/Components, Shared/Intents/Core and Shared/Resources go into all 4 targets.
- WidgetShared goes into the widget extensions.
- Shared/Intents/Siri and Shared/AppCore go into the apps.
- Platform folders hold the rest.

The rules about what may live where are enforced by lint_repo.py. Platform divergence is handled cleanly with same-named per-platform types (PlatformWidgetConfig, QuickLogView, platformPrompt()) rather than #if os in shared code.

§17 gives frozen Swift contracts for every layer: the full public SayoneCore API, HealthService, DrinkLogger, entities, intents, providers and AppModel. §18 assigns 6 engineers exclusive folders with stated dependencies and deliverables. TSV-generated string catalogs avoid JSON merge conflicts, and only one owner edits project.yml. Contracts are explicit and allow 6 parallel implementers, so the pass anchor is met.

Small contract defects, none of which tangle the design:
- primaryHandGesture() is defined in watchOS/App/HandGesture.swift but used by the watch rectangular widget view. The watch widget target does not compile watchOS/App, so this is a compile error.
- The lint rule '#if os( only in whitelisted files' conflicts with the `#if os(iOS) && SAYONE_IOS_INTENT_IN_APP` extension in QuickLogIntent, which is not whitelisted.
- Several public structs used outside the package (LastLogSnapshot for AppModel.toast, WidgetSnapshot for widget placeholders) declare no public init. Callers must go through builder APIs.
- DrinkLogger in Shared/Platform calls up into PeerSync in AppCore behind #if SAYONE_APP. That is a mild layering inversion.

The overall surface is large for an overnight build: 6 Siri intents, 2 widget kinds, controls on both platforms, WC, HealthImporter, flock, a TSV generator and a lint. The kill-switches and the M0–M5 milestones contain that risk.

criteria.rationale:
Data stays on device or in Apple services: the App Group JSON store per device, HealthKit, and WatchConnectivity between the user's own devices. There is no network, analytics or third-party service.

Usage strings (NSHealthShareUsageDescription and NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription) are in all 4 plists and localized in ru and en through InfoPlist.xcstrings.

The design avoids medical claims explicitly:
- Nutrient values are marked 'approximate, user-editable, and not medical advice'.
- The daily goal is labelled as the user's own, not a medical recommendation.
- waterPercent defaults to 100% so the app makes no hydration claims.

HealthKit scope is limited to 4 dietary quantity types (water, caffeine, energy, sugar), each tied directly to the drinks logged. Nutrient writing can be turned off. There is no health-records access, and the key is an empty array. Reading is used only to find the app's own samples (hasSamples, HealthImporter).

Minor nit: the read set could be narrowed, since the import only needs the app's own samples, and os.Logger privacy markers are not specified. Neither breaks the criterion. Everything required is present.

must_fix: Compile error: the watch rectangular widget view (§10, watchOS/Widgets/QuickLogView.swift) calls primaryHandGesture(), but that helper is defined only in watchOS/App/HandGesture.swift. The SayoneHealthWatchWidgets target compiles [watchOS/Widgets, WidgetShared, Shared/...] and not watchOS/App. Duplicate the helper, wrapped in `if #available(watchOS 11.0, *)`, into watchOS/Widgets. It cannot go in Shared or WidgetShared, because lint forbids handGestureShortcut there.

Lint conflict that fails the first linux CI job: §15.4 allows '#if os(' only in whitelisted files (DeviceOrigin.current, WidgetRefresher, PeerSync). §17.3 puts `#if os(iOS) && SAYONE_IOS_INTENT_IN_APP extension QuickLogIntent: LiveActivityIntent {}` in Shared/Intents/Core. Whitelist QuickLogIntent.swift, or move the kill-switch extension to an iOS-only folder.

Data bug, undo/save race: DrinkLogger.log saves to HealthKit outside the lock and then calls markHealth(.saved). If an undo in another process runs in between, it deletes 0 samples and marks the entry .deleted. The late markHealth(.saved) then lands on a tombstoned entry, and its sample stays in Health forever, because the flush only processes .pendingDelete. Fix: markHealth(.saved) on an isDeleted entry must set .pendingDelete and trigger a delete. Alternatively, keep pendingDelete (and do not mark .deleted when 0 were deleted) until a later flush confirms nothing exists.

Underspecified merge that can lose deletions: SyncMerge.applyImported does not say what modifiedAt imported entries get. If import time is used, the following sequence overcounts. The watch undoes X, the phone imports X from Health before the Health deletion syncs, and the WC tombstone then arrives with an older modifiedAt and loses LWW, so the phone keeps X live. Stamp imported entries with modifiedAt = entry date (or distantPast), and make tombstones win over imported (non-authoritative) copies.

StoreMaintenance.prune runs on every mutate with 7-day tombstone and 60-day retention. It must never drop entries in .pending or .pendingDelete. Otherwise an origin app that is not opened within the window leaves Health samples undeleted, or loses queued writes.

The 2 s duplicate-tap window keyed on (beverage, volume, source) also applies to source .app and Siri. A deliberate double tap on the same preset tile to log two glasses silently drops the second entry. Scope the dedupe to .widget and .control sources only.
best_ideas: Single-writer rule: only the origin device writes or deletes an entry's Health samples, and peer entries are stored as HealthSyncState.remote. This removes cross-device double counting and avoids unverified cross-source deletion.

An explicit HealthSyncState machine (pending, saved, pendingDelete, deleted, remote, skipped) with journal-first appends. Every surface uses one DrinkLogger.log path that runs in whichever process invokes it.
The flush calls hasSamples(entryID:) (metadata predicate, limit 1) before re-saving, so correctness does not depend on the undocumented equal-version re-save result.
Cross-process dedupe runs inside a flock-locked read-modify-atomic-write FileDrinkStore.mutate, which is unit-tested with concurrent writers on Linux.

HealthSamplePlanner outputs pure HealthSampleSpec values, including sync ids and metadata, tested on Linux. The Apple layer only maps them, and filters by per-kind canWrite before the all-or-nothing save([...]).

HealthImporter reads the app's own samples by SayoneEntryID metadata as a slow, guaranteed cross-device backfill. It never resurrects tombstones, because the 2-day import window is shorter than the 7-day tombstone retention.
Widget timeline dates [now, lastLog+600s, start of next day] are computed 'as of' each date, so the undo affordance expires and the midnight reset happens without extra reloads.
Same-named per-platform types (PlatformWidgetConfig, QuickLogView, platformPrompt()) instead of #if os in shared folders, with a path-scoped lint of forbidden platform APIs.
requestAuthorization is compiled only under the SAYONE_APP condition, so extensions cannot call it at all.
Frozen §17 contracts plus exclusive folder ownership for 6 engineers. String catalogs are generated from append-only TSV so parallel work never conflicts.

Compile-flag kill-switches (SAYONE_NO_WC, SAYONE_NO_WATCH_CONTROLS, SAYONE_IOS_INTENT_IN_APP) plus a Diagnostics screen (App Group shared/fallback, pending count, last sync/import) for tomorrow's device test.
A CI matrix with one leg per scheme, so each target's compile errors appear in a single round-trip. An App Intents metadata assertion checks extract.actionsdata in both apps.

criteria.rationale: I checked each requirement against a named component and flow. (1) Tap-to-log: the iPhone Today grid of preset tiles, the watch root's big primary button and one-tap rows, and every widget, control and complication button all run one single write path, DrinkLogger.log (§5.2). (2) Drink choice: a built-in catalog in §4.1 has water, sparkling water, cola-zero ('Кола без сахара / Cola Zero'), cola, coffee, tea, juice and milk. User-defined `custom-<uuid>` beverages come with a BeverageEditor, and there is a 'Другое…' tile, a Custom log sheet and a watch beverage chip in CrownVolumeView. (3) Every entry in Apple Health: HealthSamplePlanner produces flat dietaryWater/Caffeine/Energy/Sugar samples. The entry is journaled as `pending` before the Health save, and flushPendingHealth runs on launch, on becoming active and after authorization, so extension or locked-device failures are retried. The only entries not written are `skipped` ones, which the user chose or which had nothing to write. (4) Apple Watch app: a single-target watch app with Today, CrownVolumeView, ConfirmLogView, LogListView, Settings and an onboarding Health request (§13). (5) Tidy watch widget/complication: QuickLogWidget covers circular, corner, rectangular and inline, and a FavoritesWidget AccessoryWidgetGroup trio is added. §8.3 sets visual rules: containerBackground, widgetAccentable, lineLimit/minimumScaleFactor, no AccessoryWidgetBackground in a .plain label, and one widgetURL. (6) A configurable widget that logs a preset in one tap: SelectPresetIntent (a WidgetConfigurationIntent with DrinkPresetEntity?) drives QuickLogIntent, whose parameters are all pre-filled. On iPhone the user picks via Edit Widget, and promptsForUserConfiguration shows the picker when the widget is added. On the watch, before 26 each slot gets its own recommendation, and from 26 recommendations() returns [] so each instance is edited. FavoritesConfigIntent adds up to 4 slots. (7) Siri: App Intents plus AppShortcutsProvider in both apps, 6 shortcuts with ru/en phrases, parameters by preset or beverage entity, TodayTotalIntent and UndoLastDrinkIntent, and no SiriKit entitlement. Every requirement maps to a concrete component and flow, and none is vague.

must_fix: Compile error in the SayoneHealthWatchWidgets target. §10 has the Smart Stack rectangular QuickLog view call `primaryHandGesture()`, but that helper is defined only in `watchOS/App/HandGesture.swift` (§16 file tree). The watch widget extension compiles only `watchOS/Widgets, WidgetShared, Shared/*`, and the lint forbids `handGestureShortcut` in `Shared/**` and `WidgetShared/**`. So `watchOS/Widgets/QuickLogView.swift` fails with 'cannot find primaryHandGesture in scope'. Fix: define the helper (an `if #available(watchOS 11.0, *) { .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) }` wrapper) in `watchOS/Widgets` as well, or in a watch-only folder compiled into both watch targets, and give it a single owner in the §18 plan.

Watch Favorites configurability is inconsistent. §10 says Favorites 'returns one recommendation: «Избранное»' with no watchOS 26 gate, while the §8.1 matrix row 3 promises '≥ 26: 3 slots'. On watchOS 26 a non-empty recommendations() list means the system shows the preconfigured option and does not offer per-instance parameter editing. `favoritesRecommendations()` must also return [] under `#available(watchOS 26.0, *)`. The shared FavoritesConfigIntent also has slot1…slot4 while the watch trio renders 3. On watchOS 26 the editor would therefore show an unused 'Button 4'. Either add a watch-specific 3-slot config intent or document that slot4 is ignored.

iPhone systemSmall layout: §9 says 'the whole tile is one Button(intent:)' and also that 'a small ↶ button at top right appears'. If the implementer puts the ↶ UndoEntryIntent button inside the log Button's label, hit-testing between the nested widget buttons is undefined, and a tap meant to undo can log another drink instead. The spec should state that ↶ is a sibling overlay (a ZStack/overlay outside the log Button's label) with its own hit area, and the same holds for the rectangular variants.
best_ideas: A surface matrix (§8.1) that lists, for each one-tap surface, the runtime OS, the process where perform() runs, the per-instance config mechanism, the feedback and the undo path. It works both as a design checklist and as the device test plan.

A `watchTapMode` setting (instant / confirm). In confirm mode the complications render without a Button, and the root widgetURL opens a crown-adjustable ConfirmLogView that never auto-logs. This protects against accidental taps and doubles as the watchOS 10 fallback.
A widget undo window. `UndoEntryIntent` shows ↶ for 10 minutes, and a timeline entry at `lastLog + 600 s` removes it, so no reload budget is spent and the undo is visible on the widget itself.
A 2 s duplicate-tap guard evaluated inside the flock-locked store mutate, so two processes (app, widget extension, intent) cannot both append the same tap.
One `DrinkLogger.log` path for every surface: journal to the App Group store as `.pending` first, then save to HealthKit, then reload widgets. No tap is lost if the extension's HealthKit write fails.
Presets carry a `customTitle` for voice (e.g. «пол-литра воды»), which gives exact-match phrases for watch Siri, where flexible matching is unavailable.
A Favorites trio built on AccessoryWidgetGroup (watchOS 11+) with Button(intent:) slots and a Link for an empty slot, plus a medium iPhone Favorites widget with 4 configurable slots.

Per-platform same-named types (PlatformWidgetConfig, QuickLogView, `WidgetConfiguration.platformPrompt()`) instead of `#if os()` in shared code, enforced by a folder-scoped lint that forbids platform-illegal APIs (.systemSmall on watch, .accessoryCorner on iOS, promptsForUserConfiguration on watch widgets, and so on).

Relying on watchOS 26's automatic surfacing of the iPhone control on the watch (the intent never foregrounds the app), plus a native watch control gated with `#if compiler(>=6.2)` and `if #available(watchOS 26.0, *)` for the Ultra Action button.

A Health banner in the app ('N записи ждут отправки в Здоровье · Повторить') and a Diagnostics screen (App Group shared/fallback, pending count, last sync), which make tomorrow's device testing much easier.
